item.title: Summit outcomes. 2028 contenders. Jason Miller. Outage advice. Lead waste. Brewing storm. Bigfoot sightings. Catch up now.
item.description: Today’s seven most important and interesting stories.

item.title: Senate votes to weaken environmental laws in effort to speed energy projects
item.description: The bill changes decades-old laws in a bid to accelerate energy projects and make housing, roads and other infrastructure easier to build. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act passed 62-33, with 14 Democrats voting for it, including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (New York), and Sen. Angus King (I-Maine), who caucuses with Democrats. Two Republicans, Sens. Josh Hawley (Missouri) and Mike Rounds (South Dakota), voted against it.

item.title: Construction worker recalls terror as bullet struck him during Logan Circle shooting
item.description: D.C. resident Julio Majano Gonzalez said he was shot while telling other workers to take cover. The 60-year-old was one of six people Matt Lambert, a health care tech executive who had worked as an emergency room physician, shot in a rampage following a long-standing dispute over the conditions of his condominium.

item.title: White House replaces its top cybersecurity official after string of technology outages
item.description: The departure of Sean Cairncross, its national cyber director, continues the ouster of aides associated with former chief of staff Susie Wiles and comes as major outages have disrupted businesses and federal agencies.

item.title: How a child support fight exposed an unpaid Trump adviser’s $15 million income
item.description: Jason Miller’s income rose sharply after Donald Trump’s return to power, court records show. The longtime aide’s firms continued receiving payments after he began appearing more regularly at the White House.

item.title: The 41 definitive rules of hosting a dinner party
item.description: Having other humans in your home for food and drink takes effort, even as entertaining has become far less formal than in past centuries. Use these rules as guidelines for smooth, happy gatherings.

item.title: U.S. sells first-ever leases to mine the deep sea, alarming environmentalists
item.description: The Interior Department sold two leases for $6 million to mine 31 million acres of the Pacific Ocean. The sale went forward despite a court ruling that the National Marine Fisheries Service had violated the Endangered Species Act when it approved the auction.

item.title: ‘Wake up’: Rep. María Salazar tells Republicans how to fix immigration
item.description: ‘Wake up’: Rep. María Salazar tells Republicans how to fix immigration

item.title: IQ tests were built for an earlier era. Here’s the new science of what makes kids smart.
item.description: Researchers are racing to measure the skills necessary for the future.

item.title: Senate rejects resolution to block Trump from striking Iran
item.description: The vote was the first test of Republican support for the war since they lost control of Congress in the midterms.

item.title: Federal arts panel made up of Trump apppointees asks administration to rethink scope of contentious D.C. golf course redesign
item.description: The commission appeared skeptical of the plan to cut off public access to the peninsula around East Potomac Golf Links to build a championship course.

item.title: U.S. labor secretary: What type of worker are you? The choice is clear again.
item.description: Independent contractors deserve the freedom to be their own bosses.

item.title: Anthropic shares soar in debut; market value hits $2 trillion
item.description: The artificial intelligence company’s stock market IPO set a record, eclipsing the $75 billion raised by SpaceX when it went public in June, and catapulted the six-year-old company into the ranks of the world’s largest corporations alongside Meta and Walmart.

item.title: The outages keep coming. Despite government reassurances, some Americans are preparing for doomsday.
item.description: With major systems failing and explanations scarce, some are stocking up and bracing for emergencies once considered unthinkable.

item.title: Entrepreneur Mark Ein strikes deal to take over Rock Creek Tennis Center, the aging site of the DC Open
item.description: His Rollingwood Sports on Thursday announced a 60-year lease to operate the center and a commitment to invest at least $25 million.

item.title: At the border, Texans don’t hide why they turned on Trump
item.description: Immigration and economic anxiety obliterated the GOP’s 2024 gains in South Texas.

item.title: The best and worst of the CMAs: Ella Langley makes history, thanks to ‘Choosin’ Texas,’ and Taylor Swift returns
item.description: Langley scored a sweep, and Swift may have dropped a hint for fans with her wardrobe selection.

item.title: Trump, Putin and Xi met in a carefully choreographed summit that highlighted the complexity of the emerging global order
item.description: The less-than-90-minute meeting produced no major breakthroughs on the issues that mattered most to President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

item.title: We’re lonelier than ever. There’s a science-backed way to counteract that, columnist Richard Sima writes.
item.description: The inability to connect with others is a growing problem worldwide, but studies suggest there is a relatively simple solution.

item.description: Why it matters that the U.S. lost its measles-elimination status

item.title: Lifting weights on a GLP-1 is critical — but not because it saves muscle
item.description: Researchers have some of the first rigorous evidence that pumping iron is worth the effort, though perhaps not for the reason most people expect.

item.title: Hegseth makes surprise Venezuela visit, renews military partnership less than a year after U.S. capture of President Nicolás Maduro
item.description: The announcement by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth represents a major shift in the rapidly transforming U.S. relationship with Venezuela. The Venezuelan military has been under close U.S. scrutiny in recent years, and the U.S. has indicted high-ranking officers on narcotics charges.

item.title:
These are the Senate Democrats backing Van Hollen over Schumer for majority leader
BLURB
item.description: Chris Van Hollen (Maryland) is challenging Chuck Schumer (New York) in the first contested election for Senate Democratic leader in more than three decades. The winner needs support from 28 senators.

item.title: Carolyn Hax readers give advice: Brother who shunned me is back, only because he’s dying. Now what?
item.description: Beloved only sibling is now in “constant contact,” harping on the religion the letter writer was punished for leaving 50 years ago. What is the right thing to do?

item.title: Food critic Elazar Sontag takes questions — and shares one of his worst-ever dining experiences
item.description: Food critic Elazar Sontag takes questions — and shares one of his worst-ever dining experiences

item.title: Muslims to outnumber Christians as world’s largest religion by 2035, study finds
item.description: Demographic patterns suggest Christianity’s center will move to Africa, and America will no longer be majority-Christian, new research finds.

item.title: Democrat Hakeem Jeffries nominated to be the first Black speaker of the House next year
item.description: The New York Democrat prevailed with only a handful of dissenters, according to two people in the room, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to share the results of a closed-door, secret-ballot vote among House Democrats. The full House is scheduled to vote Jan. 3 on a speaker.

item.title: I said the internet would stop working. Then came the outages.
item.description: A series of tech failures in the past week are a wake-up call.

item.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ is an astonishing American epic, reviewer Gene Park writes
item.description: The game, a rags-to-riches crime odyssey in which players pilot both halves of an outlaw couple, is revolutionary because of its attention to human behavior.

item.title: Senate result. Ground stop. Pete Hegseth. Measles resurgence. AI hype. Thanksgiving forecast. GTA VI. Catch up now.
item.description: Today’s seven most important and interesting stories.

item.title: Alaska elects Mary Peltola over Sen. Dan Sullivan (R), AP reports, giving Democrats a 56-44 edge in the Senate
item.description: The race was the last to be called in the Senate, securing Democrats a historic sweep of nine new seats. Peltola, a former congresswoman, is one of two Indigenous women ever elected to the Senate.

item.title: What we know about why everything seems to be breaking at once
item.description: Microsoft’s Outlook emails, air traffic control, JPMorgan Chase and United Airlines were among the high-profile systems that had outages in the past week. Experts say the interruptions don’t seem to be connected, but everyone wants answers.

item.title: White House pulls nomination of Heidi Overton to lead Food and Drug Administration following bipartisan pushback
item.description: The decision came amid growing concerns that she could not be confirmed by the Senate to lead the agency charged with overseeing the safety of drugs, vaccines, tobacco and the majority of the U.S. food supply, according to a White House official and three other people familiar with the matter. Overton had been slated to get a vote Wednesday before a Senate committee.

item.title: How much life could a 10-minute walk buy you? Try our calculator.
item.description: Researchers calculated how spending more time moving each day may pay off in the future. See what you could gain from adding more daily movement to your life.

item.title: FAA oversaw and signed off on repair work before nationwide ground stop
item.description: A person familiar with the investigation said blame placed on contractor L3Harris overlooked the role of the Federal Aviation Administration. An FAA official was supervising a contractor in rural Arkansas as he switched vital air traffic communications lines from a old copper-wire network to a new fiber one, even testing the finished product and signing off on the work, the person said.

item.title: ICE is detaining green-card holders over decades-old, minor violations
item.description: Authorities are detaining people over charges that did not come up when applying for or renewing green cards and that in the past would have resulted in a citation — not an effort to remove legal status.

item.title: ‘The most ominous signal’: Four ways Trump may pivot after the midterm rout
item.description: Two years of a Democratic Congress might push the president to change his views.

item.title: Brazilian federal police are investigating whether JD Vance’s donor network aided Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The probe has drawn renewed attention to the uncommon political partnership between MAGA and the Bolsonaro-led Brazilian right.

item.title: National Security Agency suffers outage of internal communications system used to exchange classified messages
item.description: The reasons for the outage involving NSA Net were not immediately clear. But a former Pentagon official said it was significant enough to force the intelligence agency to delay employees’ arrival times at its headquarters at Fort Meade, Maryland, and other locations.

item.title: Behind deadly Logan Circle shooting, a familiar frustration about housing
item.description: The Logan Circle shooter had complained online and filed a lawsuit about the conditions in his D.C. condo. While his violent response is rare, his anger touched a familiar chord for Washingtonians — from renters to condo owners — who complain about festering problems that include inadequate heat, the emergence of mold and the proliferation of vermin.

item.title: Carolyn Hax: Husband dillydallies too long to make flight to friend’s wedding
item.description: Husband resisted the letter writer’s travel suggestions at every point yet insists the missed event “wasn’t on purpose.”

item.title: Jensen Huang said he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO in first remarks after resigning amid news of affair with alleged spy
item.description: The company’s founder said in a statement that he has received an outpouring of encouragement to return. Its board said Monday that it was not considering the move.

item.title: U.S. formally loses its status as a country that has eliminated measles
item.description: The designation reverses a landmark public health achievement and acknowledges a new reality: A disease Americans largely stopped having to think about for more than a quarter-century is once again spreading continuously throughout its communities.

item.title: The FAA failed. Naturally, it wants another $50 billion.
item.description: Much of the world has figured out a better way to fund air traffic control.

item.title: Trump pushes more White House renovations in wake of GOP midterm loss
item.description: The president has claimed he is paying for the White House makeover, but the Park Service is set to foot much of the bill.

item.title: Lawyers for Saudi national accused of bugging OpenAI say there’s no evidence he’s a spy
item.description: Abdulrahman Alfozan, who worked as an engineer at OpenAI, was arrested last month and charged with one count of violating the Wiretap Act for allegedly placing a recording device behind a TV in an executive conference room at the AI company. Prosecutors have not provided any evidence that Alfozan has ties to the Saudi government or was working at its behest, despite providing a set of documents and engaging in two meetings with defense lawyers, Alfozan’s lawyers said in a filing Monday.

item.title: We have a new James Bond. But are we happy about it?
item.description: What’s in store for the next James Bond movie now that director Denis Villeneuve has ended years of rampant speculation and cast the idiosyncratic Robert Pattinson as 007? We have thoughts.
